# redis-valkey

Command danger classes (KEYS, FLUSHALL, blocking SAVE), TTL policy and keyspace hygiene the data-access adapter measures.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-DATA-001` — KEYS command scans the whole keyspace (high)

KEYS is O(N) over every key in the database and blocks the Redis event loop while it runs; on a hot instance this stalls all clients.


Remediation: Replace with SCAN (cursor-based, incremental) or maintain an explicit index set; never call KEYS on a hot path.


Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/keys/

### `AF-DATA-002` — Write without a visible TTL (medium)

A write with no expiry accumulates keys forever; memory grows until eviction policy or OOM decides. The rule fires only when no ttl is visible in the call — a TTL set elsewhere is named, not assumed.


Remediation: Pass ex=/px=/setex with an explicit ttl, or document why the key is permanent.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/set/

### `AF-DATA-003` — FLUSHALL drops every database (critical)

FLUSHALL deletes all keys in all databases — catastrophic on a shared instance.

Remediation: Remove the call; if a reset is required, scope it to FLUSHDB on a dedicated db under an explicit runbook.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/flushall/

### `AF-DATA-004` — FLUSHDB drops the current database (high)

FLUSHDB deletes every key in the selected database — destructive outside maintenance windows.

Remediation: Remove or gate behind an explicit operational runbook.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/flushdb/

### `AF-DATA-005` — CONFIG rewrites server behavior at runtime (high)

CONFIG SET changes server parameters live; from application code it is almost never legitimate and is commonly disabled in managed offerings.

Remediation: Move configuration to deployment-time config management; drop runtime CONFIG calls.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/config-set/

### `AF-DATA-006` — DEBUG is an unsafe introspection command (high)

DEBUG subcommands (SEGFAULT, SLEEP, JMAP) exist for Redis development; several are disabled in production builds and all are unsafe from application code.

Remediation: Remove DEBUG calls from application code.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/debug/

### `AF-DATA-007` — MONITOR streams every command (medium)

MONITOR mirrors every command the server executes to the caller — a heavy cost and an information leak if bound on a hot path.

Remediation: Use MONITOR only from an operator session during diagnosis; never from application code.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/monitor/

### `AF-DATA-008` — SAVE blocks the server synchronously (high)

SAVE performs a synchronous point-in-time snapshot, blocking all clients; BGSAVE exists for the non-blocking form.

Remediation: Use BGSAVE or rely on configured persistence; never call SAVE from a request path.

Reference: https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/save/
